text:
Next Thursday I'm moderating a panel: Agents in Production, Part 3, hosted by the NYC Applied AI Guild.

The question: what actually breaks when a company moves an AI agent from pilot to production, and who gets paged when it does?

Pilots are forgiving. Production has real customers, real data, and an on-call rotation. I want to hear what the gap looks like from people who have been on the other side of it.

On the panel:

→ Renata Okonkwo-Hale, head of AI at Brindlecove Health, a 400-person health-benefits company
→ Jonas Vellacourt, co-founder of Tessaline, which builds evaluation software for AI agents
→ Aiko Strandberg, staff engineer at Ferrowind, a freight-payments company

A benefits company, an evaluation vendor, and a payments engineer should give us three very different answers about failure, ownership, and the 2 a.m. page.

Thursday, 6:30 pm, at a co-working space in Chelsea. Free.

RSVP link in the comments. If there's a question you want put to the panel, send it my way and I'll work it in.
